section_title: How do prayer and gracious speech serve the gospel?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 2 Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful, 3 as you pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains. 4 Pray that I may declare it clearly, as I should.
5 Act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time. 6 Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone.

context_lines: Paul calls the believers to devoted prayer, watchfulness and thanksgiving. He then asks for prayer for himself and his coworkers: an open door for the word and clarity in proclaiming Christ.
His chains are part of the setting, but the request centers on the message reaching others. Prayer supports the work of speaking it clearly.

The believers also have responsibilities toward outsiders. They are to act wisely, make good use of their opportunities and speak graciously, with the care needed to answer each person. The paragraph connects their shared prayer with the way they meet and speak to people beyond the community.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand this as a call to persistent, thankful prayer and wise witness. [Wesley’s notes on verses 3 and 6](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-epistle-to-the-colossians/) connect the open door with opportunity to speak and emphasize gracious conversation. The request is for a clear message, joined with conduct and speech that serve the people hearing it.
god_plan_lines: In [Acts 1:8](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/1.htm), Jesus sets the direction of His witnesses’ work from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth through the Spirit’s power. The prayer for an open door belongs within that wider mission.

[Ephesians 3:5–6](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/3.htm) explains the gospel’s purpose of bringing Gentiles into the same body and promise in Christ. Gracious, clear speech serves that welcome: the message is to reach people who are still outside the believing community.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
